text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- The the mark's fall of against the dollar on the international markets will not affect Bulgaria's export potential, Prime minister Ivan Kostov said.
-- Bulgaria's East Orthodox Church has its first web page in Internet.
-- Bulgarian customs officers said they had seized 162 tonnes of imported U.S. boneless beef meat. The meat had no certificates for origin and shelf life labels.

-- Bulgaria's police said an Italian businessman Egidio Fruli was beaten to death in a night club in central Sofia. Visiting Italian deputies said Fruli was suspected in involvement in Albanian pyramid investment schemes.

-- Bulgaria may export 3,200 tonnes of lamb meat to the European Union until the end of this year under a quota agreement for exports of Bulgarian live lambs and meat to the EU, deputy Trade minister Alexander Tasev said.
Bulgaria's quota for lamb exports to the EU totals 5,288 tonnes.
-- Bulgaria's Foreign minister Nadezhda Mihailova discussed with her visiting Croatian counterpart Mate Granic possible trade liberalisation between the two Balkan countries.
-- The Bulgarian National Bank's (BNB) chief legal adviser Borislav Stratev resigned, BNB's governor Svetoslav Gavriiski said but declined to elaborate Stratev's motives.
-- The Bulgarian National Bank said it would place in circulation 50 levs coins from August 1 to replace notes which will be withdrawn from circulation by July 31 next year.

-- Bulgaria's President Petar Stoyanov is expected to start on Thursday a second round of talks on the new country's coat of arms with representative of the parliamentary parties, President's presscentre said.
-- Bulgaria may seek a new debt rating by the end of this year and the country may issue Eurobonds in the beginning of 1998, Bulgarian National Bank's governor Svetoslav Gavriiski said.

-- Bulgaria should restructure its education system to set up secondary schools for extramural students as many of them are forced to quit education and start working, Bulgarian Teachers' Trade Union said.
Some 15,000 Bulgarian students left secondary schools last year. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
